title: Statutory Obligations of the Person in Charge
summary: This thread covers the foundational legal duties of the person in charge of a conveyance, including arrival reporting, emergency protocols, and liability for non-compliance. These provisions remain largely static, representing the core legal framework of the Customs Act that governs the physical movement and custody of conveyances.

evolution.legal_basis: Remains consistent as the primary statutory authority for conveyance management.

timeline.change: Establishment of core legal duties and liabilities.

Customs Station: This location is the only designated place where a vehicle arriving from outside Bangladesh is permitted to dock or land. Unauthorized docking or landing at any other location is prohibited unless under specific emergency circumstances.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is strictly prohibited from docking or landing at any place other than a customs station, except in cases of accident, bad weather, or unavoidable necessity.
In cases of emergency, the person in charge must immediately report the arrival to the nearest customs officer or police station and provide access to the manifest, log-book, or cargo book.

The person in charge must ensure that no cargo is offloaded and no crew member or passenger leaves the site without the explicit consent of the customs officer, unless such actions are necessary to protect life, health, or property.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: An officer of customs is empowered to oversee vessels or vehicles that are forced to land at non-customs stations due to emergencies.

The officer has the authority to issue instructions regarding the handling of cargo, and their consent is required before any goods are offloaded or any crew or passengers are allowed to depart from the site of an emergency landing.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Conveyance returning to customs-station may enter and land goods
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
136. Conveyance returning to customs-station may enter and land goods.- (1) In either of the cases mentioned in section 135, the person-in-charge of the conveyance may enter such conveyance inwards and any owner of goods thereon may, with the consent of the person-in-charge of conveyance, land the same under the provisions of this Act and the rules.
(2) In every such case, any export duty paid shall be refunded on an application made by the owner of such goods within one year of their landing and any amount paid to owners as drawback or repayment of duty (whether of customs, excise or any other tax) shall be recovered from him or adjusted against the amount refundable.

Conveyance: If a conveyance is forced to return to a customs-station, the person in charge may enter the conveyance inwards after its return.
When a conveyance returns to a customs-station, the owner of the goods on board may land the goods provided they have the consent of the person in charge of the conveyance.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance that has returned to a customs-station has the authority to enter the conveyance inwards.
The person in charge of a conveyance controls whether or not the owners of goods on board are permitted to land their goods upon returning to a customs-station.
Export Duty: If goods are landed after a conveyance returns to a customs-station, any export duty previously paid on those goods is eligible for a refund.
Customs Duty Drawback: If a refund is claimed for goods landed after a conveyance returns, any previously issued drawback or tax repayment related to those goods must be recovered from the owner or adjusted against the refund amount.
Customs Station: This station serves as the location where a returning conveyance may enter inwards and where goods on board may be landed by their owners.

static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
137. Landing of goods during repairs.- (1) The appropriate officer may, on application by the person-in-charge of a conveyance which is obliged before completing her journey or voyage to put into any customs-station for repairs, permit him to land the goods or any portion thereof, and to place it in the custody of an officer of customs during such repairs, and to load and export the same free of duty.
(2) All expenses attending such custody shall be borne by the person-in- charge of the conveyance.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the discretionary authority to permit the offloading of goods from a conveyance that has arrived at a customs station for necessary repairs prior to completing its journey.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge may apply to the appropriate officer for permission to land goods when their conveyance requires repairs at a customs station.
The person in charge is responsible for bearing all expenses related to the custody of the goods during the period of repair.
Customs Custody: Goods landed for the purpose of conveyance repairs are required to be placed under the custody of an officer of customs.
Export of Goods: Goods that were landed for the purpose of repairs may be re-loaded and exported without the payment of customs duty.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Frustrated cargo and other than frustrated cargo how dealt with
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
138. Frustrated cargo 31[and other than frustrated cargo] how dealt with.- (1) Where any goods are brought into a customs-station by reason of inadvertence, mis-direction or untraceability of the consignee, the 1[Commissioner of Customs] may, on application by the person-in-charge of the conveyance which brought such goods or of the consignor of such goods and subject to rules, allow export of such goods without payment of any duties (whether of import or export) chargeable thereon, provided that such goods have remained and are exported under the custody of an officer of customs.
32[(1A) Where any goods are brought into a customs-station by a reason other than the reasons mentioned in sub-section (1), the Commissioner of Customs may, with prior approval of the Board, allow re-exportation of such goods without payment of any duties chargeable thereon.]
(2) All expenses attending to such custody shall be borne by the applicant.

Frustrated Cargo: Frustrated cargo refers to goods brought into a customs station due to inadvertence, misdirection, or the untraceability of the consignee. The Commissioner of Customs may permit the export of such goods without payment of import or export duties, provided the goods remain under customs custody until their departure.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is authorized to approve the export of frustrated cargo upon application by the person in charge of the conveyance or the consignor, subject to established rules and the condition of maintaining customs custody.

For goods brought into a customs station under circumstances other than those classified as frustrated cargo, the Commissioner of Customs may authorize re-exportation without duty payment, provided prior approval from the National Board of Revenue is obtained.
Customs Station: A customs station serves as the designated location for the management and handling of frustrated cargo and other goods eligible for re-exportation.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance that brought goods into a customs station may apply to the Commissioner of Customs for the export of frustrated cargo without payment of duties.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue must provide prior approval before the Commissioner of Customs can authorize the re-exportation of goods that do not meet the legal criteria for frustrated cargo.
Customs Custody: Goods designated for export as frustrated cargo must remain under the continuous custody of an officer of customs throughout the process to qualify for duty exemptions.
All expenses incurred while goods are held in customs custody must be paid by the applicant who requested the export or re-exportation.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Levy of penalty for departure without authority or failure to bring-to
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
183. Levy of penalty for departure without authority or failure to bring-to.- (1) If any conveyance actually departs without a port clearance or permission in writing or, in the case of a vessel, after having failed to bring-to when required at any station appointed under section 14, the penalty to which the person-in-charge of such conveyance is liable may be adjudged by the appropriate officer of any customs-station, to which such conveyance proceeds, or in which it for the time being is.
(2) A certificate in respect of such departure or failure to bring-to when required, purporting to be signed by the appropriate officer of the customs-station from which the conveyance is stated to have so departed, shall be prima facie proof of the fact so stated.

Conveyance: A conveyance that departs without required port clearance or written permission, or a vessel that fails to bring-to as instructed at an appointed station, is subject to specific penalty provisions.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer at any customs station where the conveyance is found or proceeds has the authority to adjudge penalties against the person in charge for unauthorized departure or failure to bring-to.
A signed certificate issued by an officer at the customs station of departure serves as evidence regarding the occurrence of the unauthorized departure or failure to comply with instructions.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is held liable for penalties if the conveyance departs without proper authorization or fails to follow lawful instructions to bring-to at a station.
Burden of Proof: A certificate issued by the appropriate customs officer confirming a violation acts as evidence for the facts stated therein regarding the conveyance's departure or failure to bring-to.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Liability of agent appointment by the person-in-charge of a conveyance
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
210. Liability of agent appointment by the person-in-charge of a conveyance.- (1) Anything which the person-in-charge of a conveyance is required or empowered to do under this Act may, with the express or implied consent of the person-in-charge and the approval of the appropriate officer, be done by his agent.

(2) An agent appointed by the person-in-charge of a conveyance, and any person who represents himself to any officer of customs as an agent of any such person-in-charge and is accepted as such by that officer, shall be liable for the fulfilment in respect of the matter in question of all obligations imposed on such person-in-charge by or under this Act or any law for the time being in force, and to penalties ( including confiscation) which may be incurred in respect of that matter.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is permitted to authorize an agent to perform actions required or empowered under the Customs Act.
They retain ultimate responsibility for obligations and liabilities, but may delegate the performance of these duties with the approval of an appropriate customs officer.
Agent: An agent may act on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance provided they have the express or implied consent of the person in charge and approval from an appropriate officer.
An agent, or anyone representing themselves as an agent and accepted by an officer, assumes full legal liability for all obligations imposed on the person in charge of the conveyance.
Agents are subject to all penalties, including the confiscation of goods or vehicles, related to the matters they handle for the person in charge.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to approve the appointment of an agent acting on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance.
They have the authority to formally accept a person who represents themselves as an agent, thereby binding that person to the legal obligations and liabilities of the person in charge.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance
Agent: person in charge of a conveyance
Appropriate Officer of Customs: person in charge of a conveyance

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance entering Bangladesh from abroad is legally mandated to ensure the conveyance first arrives only at a designated customs station.

In cases of emergency, such as accidents or unavoidable circumstances forcing an arrival elsewhere, the person in charge must immediately report the arrival to the nearest customs officer or police station.

During emergency arrivals, the person in charge must produce relevant transport documents like the cargo book, manifest, or log-book upon request and must not permit the unloading of goods or the departure of passengers or crew without official consent.
The person in charge is obligated to comply with all directions provided by customs or police officers regarding the goods onboard during emergency situations.
Customs Station: A customs station is the mandatory first point of arrival for any conveyance entering Bangladesh from outside the country.
Officer of Customs: Customs officers have the authority to receive reports of emergency arrivals, inspect conveyance documents, and provide binding directions regarding the handling of goods, passengers, and crew.
Officer-in-charge of Police Station: In the event of an emergency landing at a location other than a customs station, the officer-in-charge of the police station may receive arrival reports and exercise oversight similar to a customs officer until further authority is established.
Passenger or Crew: Passengers and crew members are restricted from leaving the vicinity of a conveyance that has made an emergency landing at a non-customs location without the consent of a customs or police officer.
Departures from the conveyance are permitted without prior consent only when necessary for urgent reasons of health, safety, or the preservation of life and property.
Goods: Goods transported by a conveyance forced into an emergency landing at a non-customs location cannot be unloaded without authorization, and their handling is subject to the directives of the relevant customs or police authorities.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Delivery of import manifest in respect of a conveyance other than a vessel
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text: 44. Delivery of import manifest in respect of a conveyance other than a vessel.- The person-in-charge of a conveyance other than a vessel shall, within twenty-four hours after arrival thereof at a land customs-station or customs- airport, as the case may be, deliver an import manifest to the appropriate officer 4[or if the person-in-charge is a registered user, he may transmit the manifest to the Customs computer system].

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance that is not a vessel must deliver an import manifest to the appropriate officer within a specific timeframe after reaching a customs station or customs airport.
A registered user acting as the person in charge may fulfill their obligation by transmitting the manifest electronically to the customs computer system.
Land Customs Station: This location serves as a point of arrival where the person in charge of a non-vessel conveyance must submit an import manifest.
Customs Airport: This location serves as a point of arrival where the person in charge of a non-vessel conveyance must submit an import manifest.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is the designated recipient of the import manifest delivered by the person in charge of a conveyance upon its arrival.
Import Manifest: This document is required to be delivered by the person in charge of a conveyance to the appropriate officer or transmitted electronically via the customs computer system upon arrival at a customs station.
Registered User: A registered user has the authority to submit import manifests by transmitting them to the customs computer system rather than through manual delivery.
Customs Computerised System: This system is used by registered users to electronically transmit import manifests to fulfill customs arrival obligations.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Signature and contents of import manifest and amendment thereof
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
45. Signature and contents of import manifest and amendment thereof.- (1) Every manifest delivered under section 43 or section 44 shall be signed by the person-in-charge of the conveyance or his duly authorised agent and shall specify all goods imported in such conveyance showing separately all goods, if any, intended to be landed, transhipped, transited or taken on to another customs-station or to a destination outside 1[Bangladesh] and stores intended for consumption at the customs-station or in the outward voyage or journey, and shall be made out in such form and contain such further particulars as the Board may from time to time direct 2[:]
3[Provided that the manifest transmitted to the Customs computer system by a registered user shall be deemed to have been signed by him.]
(2) The appropriate officer shall permit the person-in-charge of a conveyance or his duly authorised agent to correct any obvious error in the import manifest or to supply any omission which in the opinion of such officer results from accident or inadvertence, by furnishing an amended or supplementary import manifest and shall levy thereon such fees as the Board from time to time directs.
4[(3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (2), the Board may specify, by special Order, the manner, conditions, limitations or restrictions under which the appropriate officer shall permit the person-in-charge of a conveyance, or his duly authorised agent, to submit an amended or supplementary import manifest in special circumstances and shall levy thereon such fees as the Board may direct.]

Import Manifest: The import manifest must be signed by the person in charge of the conveyance or their authorized agent and must specify all goods imported, categorizing them by their intended status such as landed, transhipped, or destined for another station or country.
The manifest must include stores intended for consumption and be prepared in the form and with the particulars as directed by the National Board of Revenue.

The person in charge of a conveyance or their authorized agent may be permitted to correct obvious errors or omissions in an import manifest by submitting an amended or supplementary version, subject to fees directed by the National Board of Revenue.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance or their authorized agent is responsible for signing and delivering the import manifest and providing any necessary amendments or supplementary documentation to the appropriate officer.
Agent: A duly authorized agent may sign and deliver an import manifest or submit amendments and supplementary information on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the form and particulars of the import manifest, determine the fees for amendments or supplements, and issue special orders regarding the conditions and limitations for submitting such amendments in special circumstances.
Registered User: An import manifest transmitted to the customs computer system by a registered user is legally deemed to have been signed by that user.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is empowered to allow corrections of obvious errors or omissions in the import manifest and to impose prescribed fees for the processing of amended or supplementary manifests.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance
Agent: person in charge of a conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Power to require production of documents and ask questions
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
48. Power to require production of documents and ask questions.- (1) When an import manifest is presented, the person-in-charge of a conveyance or his duly authorised agent, if required so to do by the appropriate officer, shall deliver to the officer the bill of lading or the bill of freight or a copy thereof for every part of cargo or goods laden or board, journey log-book and any port clearance, docket or other paper granted in respect of such conveyance at the place from which it is stated to have come, and shall answer all such questions relating to the conveyance, goods, crew7[, passengers] and voyage or journey as are put to him by such officer.
(2) The appropriate officer may, if any requisition or question made or put by him under this section is not complied with or answered, refuse to grant permission to a vessel to break bulk and to other conveyance to land the imported goods, as the case may be.

Import Manifest: The presentation of an import manifest triggers the authority of customs officers to request specific documents and information from the person in charge of a conveyance.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance or their authorized agent is legally obligated to produce transport documents and answer questions regarding the cargo, crew, passengers, and journey upon request by an appropriate officer of customs.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs has the authority to demand production of shipping documents and to pose questions to the person in charge of a conveyance.
The officer is empowered to refuse permission for a vessel to break bulk or for other conveyances to land imported goods if their requisitions for documents or answers to questions are not satisfied.
Bill of Lading: The person in charge of a conveyance must deliver the bill of lading or a copy thereof for the cargo upon the request of an appropriate officer of customs.
Port Clearance: The person in charge of a conveyance must produce port clearance and other related papers issued at the point of origin when required by an appropriate officer of customs.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Order for entry outwards or loading of goods to be obtained before export goods are loaded
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
50. Order for entry outwards or loading of goods to be obtained before export goods are loaded.- (1) No goods other than passengers baggage and mail bags shall be loaded on a conveyance until-
(a) in the case of a vessel, a written application for entry of such vessel outwards, subscribed by the master of such vessel has been made to the appropriate officer and an order has been given thereon for such entry; and
(b) in the case of any other conveyance, a written application for authority to load the goods subscribed by the person-in-charge of the conveyance has been made to the appropriate officer and an order has been given thereon authorising the loading.
(2) Every application made under this section shall specify the particulars as prescribed by the Board.

Export Goods: No goods, excluding passenger baggage and mail bags, may be loaded onto a conveyance for export until specific regulatory requirements for entry or loading authorization have been satisfied.
Vessel: A vessel is subject to a mandatory entry outward process, requiring the master to submit a written application to the appropriate officer and obtain an order for entry before any export goods can be loaded.
Vessel Master: The master of a vessel is responsible for submitting a formal written application for entry outwards to the appropriate officer to facilitate the legal loading of export goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is the authority responsible for receiving written applications and issuing the necessary orders for the entry of vessels or authorization for the loading of other conveyances.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: For conveyances other than vessels, the person in charge must submit a written application for loading authorization to the appropriate officer to ensure legal compliance before loading goods.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the specific particulars that must be included in applications for vessel entry or conveyance loading authorization under this section.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Conveyances other than vessels to deliver documents and answer question before departure
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
54. Conveyances other than vessels to deliver documents and answer question before departure.- The person-in-charge of a conveyance other than a vessel or his duly authorised agent shall-
(a) deliver to the appropriate officer an export manifest in duplicate in such form as may from time to time be prescribed by the Board signed by such person-in-charge or the agent specifying all goods or stores entered in the import manifest, and not landed or transhipped or consumed on board the conveyance;
(b) deliver to the appropriate officer such bills of export or other documents as such officer acting under the general instructions of the 1[Commissioner of Customs] requires; and
(c) answer such questions respecting the departure and destination of the conveyance as are put to him by the appropriate officer.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance, other than a vessel, or their authorized agent is legally obligated to perform specific procedural tasks before the departure of the conveyance.

They must provide the appropriate officer with an export manifest in the prescribed form, submit necessary bills of export or other required documentation, and respond to inquiries regarding the conveyance's departure and destination.
Agent: An agent may act on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance to fulfill legal requirements for document delivery and manifest submission before departure.
Export Manifest: The person in charge of a conveyance must deliver an export manifest in duplicate to the appropriate officer.
This document must be signed and detail all goods or stores that were included in the import manifest but were not landed, transhipped, or consumed during the transit.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is the designated authority to receive the export manifest, bills of export, and other required documents from the person in charge of the conveyance.
They are also authorized to question the person in charge regarding the conveyance's departure and destination.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the form for the export manifest that must be submitted by the person in charge of the conveyance.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs provides the general instructions under which the appropriate officer requires the submission of specific bills of export and additional documentation.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance
Agent: person in charge of a conveyance
Appropriate Officer of Customs: person in charge of the conveyance
National Board of Revenue: person in charge of the conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Grant of port-clearance or permission for departure
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text: 56. Grant of port-clearance or permission for departure.- When the appropriate officer is satisfied that the provisions of this Chapter relating to the departure of conveyances have been duly complied with, he shall grant a port- clearance to the master of the vessel or a written permission for departure to the person-in-charge of any other conveyance and shall return at the same time to such master or person-in-charge one copy of the manifest duly countersigned by the appropriate officer.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is responsible for verifying that all legal requirements concerning the departure of a conveyance have been satisfied before authorizing its departure.
Port Clearance: This document is granted to the master of a vessel by the appropriate officer once all departure requirements are met.
Departure Permission: This written authorization is issued to the person-in-charge of a conveyance, other than a vessel, upon the fulfillment of all necessary departure formalities.
Master of the Vessel: The master must receive port clearance and a countersigned copy of the manifest from the appropriate officer before the vessel is permitted to depart.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: This person must obtain written permission for departure from the appropriate officer, along with a countersigned copy of the manifest, after ensuring all regulatory compliance for departure.
Manifest: A copy of the manifest must be countersigned by the appropriate officer and returned to the master or person-in-charge of the conveyance upon the granting of departure permission.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Power to cancel port-clearance or permission for departure
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
58. Power to cancel port-clearance or permission for departure.- (1) For the purpose of securing compliance with any provision of this Act or the rules or any other law, the appropriate officer may at any time, while the vessel is within the limits of any port or any other conveyance is within the limits of any station or airport or within 1[Bangladesh] territory, demand the return of port- clearance or the written permission for departure, as the case may be.
(2) Any such demand may be made in writing or may be communicated to the person-in-charge of the conveyance by wireless, and if made in writing it may be served-
(a) by delivery to the person-in-charge or his agent personally; or
(b) by leaving it at the last known place of abode of such person or agent; or
(c) by leaving it on board the conveyance with the person appearing to be in charge or command thereof.
(3) Where a demand for the return of a port-clearance or of a permission for departure is made as aforesaid, the port-clearance or permission shall forthwith become void.

Port Clearance: The appropriate officer may demand the return of a port clearance for the purpose of securing compliance with the Customs Act or other relevant laws while a vessel is within port limits or Bangladesh territory.
A port clearance becomes immediately void once a valid demand for its return has been made by the appropriate officer.
Departure Permission: The appropriate officer is empowered to demand the return of written permission for departure from a conveyance while it is located within a customs station, airport, or Bangladeshi territory.
Once a formal demand for the return of a departure permission is issued, the document is legally rendered void.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to secure legal compliance by demanding the return of port clearance or departure permission from conveyances located within their jurisdiction.
The officer may issue these demands in writing or via wireless communication to the person in charge of the conveyance.
Conveyance: When located within the limits of a station, airport, or Bangladeshi territory, a conveyance is subject to the authority of customs officers regarding the cancellation of departure permissions.
Demands for the return of clearance documents may be served by leaving the notice on board the conveyance with the person currently in command.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is the recipient of any demand for the return of clearance or departure permissions, which may be delivered personally, left at their last known residence, or communicated via wireless.
They are responsible for complying with the demand, following which their current clearance or departure permission becomes void.
Agent: A written demand for the return of port clearance or departure permission may be legally served by delivering the notice to the agent of the person in charge of the conveyance.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: person in charge of the conveyance
Person in Charge of Conveyance: person in charge of a conveyance
Agent: person in charge of the conveyance

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Officer to be received and accommodation to be provided
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text: 61. Officer to be received and accommodation to be provided.- Whenever an officer of customs is so deputed to be on board any conveyance, the person-in-charge shall be bound to receive him on board and to provide him with suitable accommodation and adequate quantity of fresh water.

Officer of Customs: When an officer of customs is assigned to be on board a conveyance, they must be received by the person in charge.
The officer is entitled to receive suitable accommodation and an adequate supply of fresh water while on board.
Conveyance: A conveyance must accommodate assigned customs officers and provide them with fresh water when they are deputed to be on board.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is legally bound to receive assigned customs officers and ensure they are provided with suitable accommodation and fresh water.

static_replicated_objects.clause_title: Discharge of goods by conveyances other than vessels
static_replicated_objects.resolved_text: 74. Discharge of goods by conveyances other than vessels.- When on arrival of a conveyance other than a vessel at a land customs-station or customs- airport the person-in-charge of such conveyance has delivered the import manifest under section 44 and the documents required under section 48, he shall forthwith take the conveyance or cause it to be taken to the examination station at the land customs-station or customs-airport and remove or cause to be removed all goods carried in such conveyance to the custom-house in the presence of the appropriate officer or some person duly authorised by him in that behalf.

Conveyance: Upon arrival at a customs station or customs airport, the person in charge must move the conveyance to the designated examination station after fulfilling initial manifest and documentation requirements.
Customs Station: The person in charge of a conveyance is required to take the vehicle to the examination station located at the customs station for the purpose of discharging goods.
Customs Airport: Upon arrival, the person in charge must proceed to the examination station at the customs airport to facilitate the removal and discharge of goods.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: Following the delivery of the import manifest and required documents, this person must ensure the conveyance is moved to the examination station and that all goods are transferred to the custom house under official supervision.
Import Manifest: The delivery of this document is a mandatory prerequisite for the person in charge to proceed with the movement of the conveyance and the discharge of goods.
Customs Documents: The person in charge must submit all required documents under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969 before initiating the discharge of goods.
Customs House: Goods carried by a conveyance must be removed and transported to this location in the presence of an appropriate officer or an authorized person.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The removal of goods from a conveyance to the custom house must be conducted in the presence of this officer or a person duly authorized by them.

static_replicated_objects.resolved_text:
78. Power to permit immediate discharge.- (1) Notwithstanding anything contended in sections 74, 76 and 77, the appropriate officer in any customs-station to which the Board, by notification in the official Gazette, declares this section to apply, may permit the master of any vessel immediately on receipt of an order under section 47 or a special pass under section 49, or the person-in-charge of a conveyance other than a vessel on receipt of the import manifest to discharge the goods imported by such conveyance, or any portion thereof, into the custody of his agent, if he be willing to receive the same, for the purpose of unloading the same forthwith-
(a) at the custom-house, or at any specified landing-place or wharf; or
(b) at any landing-place or wharf belonging to the port commissioners, port trust, railways or other public body or company; or
(c) for giving it in the custody of such person as may be approved by the 2[Commissioner of Customs].
(2) Any agent so receiving such cargo or portion shall be bound to discharge all claims for damage or short delivery which may be established in respect of the same by the owner thereof, and shall be entitled to recover from such owner his charges for service rendered, but not for commission or the like, where any agent for the unloading of such cargo or portion has been previously appointed by the owner and such appointment is unrevoked 1[:
Provide that no agent so receiving such cargo or portion shall cause it to be removed or otherwise dealt with except in accordance with the written order of the appropriate officer.]
(3) The appropriate officer shall take charge of all goods discharged under clause (a) of sub-section (1) and otherwise proceed in relation thereto as provided in section 76 and 82.
(4) 2[A public body or company or port authority or airlines or] person at whose landing- place or wharf or place of storage any goods are discharged under clause (b) or clause (c) of sub-section (1) shall not permit the same to be removed or otherwise dealt with except in accordance with the order in writing of the appropriate officer.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to permit the immediate discharge of goods from a vessel or conveyance into the custody of an agent, provided the customs-station has been declared applicable for this section by the Board.

This officer is responsible for managing the custody of goods discharged at custom-houses and ensuring that goods discharged at authorized landing places or warehouses are not removed or dealt with without written authorization.
The officer must proceed with the handling of discharged goods in accordance with the prescribed sections of the Customs Act 1969.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the power to designate specific customs-stations where the provision for immediate discharge of goods may be applied through a notification in the official Gazette.
Master of the Vessel: The master of a vessel may be permitted to immediately discharge imported goods upon receiving a valid arrival order or a special pass.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance other than a vessel is authorized to discharge imported goods upon receipt of the import manifest, subject to the permission of the appropriate officer.
Agent: An agent may receive imported goods for immediate discharge if they are willing to do so, assuming legal responsibility for claims related to damage or short delivery.

The agent is entitled to recover service charges from the owner of the goods but is prohibited from removing or dealing with the cargo except as permitted by the written order of the appropriate officer.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is authorized to approve the specific persons permitted to hold goods in custody under the immediate discharge provisions.
Port Authority: Port authorities, public bodies, or companies providing landing places or storage are prohibited from allowing the removal or handling of discharged goods without the written order of the appropriate officer.
Imported Goods: Imported goods may be discharged immediately into the custody of an agent at approved locations such as custom-houses, wharves, or other public body storage facilities to facilitate prompt unloading.
